*.text: Michigan context. Amalia Llano finished her own Michigan pass on October 23, 2026; this is a full update on top of her edits, so re-check every field and look for what is still missing rather than repeating her sources. The utility regulator is the Michigan Public Service Commission, with cases numbered like U-21090; its docket site is mi-psc.my.site.com. Air permits come from the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) Air Quality Division: a Permit to Install (PTI) for new turbines or engines, a Renewable Operating Permit (Michigan's Title V permit) for large plants, and a State Registration Number (SRN) that joins them. Read the harvested permit index in work/permits/us-mi/<plant id>.md and the dockets and queue entries on this brief first. Most of the state is in MISO; the southwest corner (Indiana Michigan Power) is in PJM. Every unit is missing Equipment Manufacturer/Model and Latest Activity: fill both wherever a permit, filing or company page names the turbine or engine make and model or gives a dated milestone. Statewide leads from the Public Service Commission dockets: the DTE Superior Peaking Station (retiring 2032, not in GEM), the Livingston Generating Station in Gaylord (bought by Consumers in 2025, not in GEM), the River Rouge peakers 11-1 to 11-4 (retired 2024), and the Upper Peninsula Power Gladstone oil turbine. Check each against the threshold and the eight EIA plants GEM lacks.

L100000409227.text: Amalia Llano merged the two Holland records on 2026-10-23, so this plant now holds the one unit 9 (83.5 MW, 2000). Do not stage a duplicate question. Check that the merged record is right: the unit still exists, the capacity and start year match EIA-860 and the EGLE permit for the 48th Street Peaking Station (SRN N2586), and the status is still operating since Holland energy park opened in 2017. Fill the turbine make and model and Latest Activity from the permit.

L100000402478.text: Midland Cogeneration Venture. EIA-860M for September 2026 gives 1468.6 MW nameplate for the generators GEM counts as unit 1, GEM says 1849 MW; check whether GEM counts steam or summer and winter ratings and record the nameplate generating MW. Unit 2 is a 380 MW fuel oil unit marked mothballed: confirm with a dated source whether it is mothballed, retired or operating, and check for any restart. Check the owner: GEM says Midland Cogeneration Venture LP with Capital Power as parent; confirm current shares against EIA-860 ownership tables and company releases.

L100000401829.text: Dan E Karn power station. Units 3 and 4 (oil and gas) have a planned retirement of 2031 in GEM. Confirm the date in the Consumers Energy plan (Case U-21090 settlement and the 2026 plan filing), and whether the 2026 plan or any federal order moved it. Karn 1 and 2 are coal and were due to retire in 2023: check whether either was kept on under a Department of Energy emergency order like Campbell, and whether any conversion to gas is proposed.

L100000103973.text: Belle River coal-to-gas conversion. The validation report says the plant's location has no Location Data Source: find a document that gives the site (the EGLE permit, the EIA-860 plant table address, or a satellite look) and stage the location source. Check the conversion milestones: Unit 1 timepoint 2 operating since 2026 and Unit 2 timepoint 2 under construction. Find dated sources for each unit's gas start, and retire or update the coal timepoint 1 units to match. A closed database comment from Jeanette Lim says Unit 1 converted in 2025; settle the year. Two saved copies of the EGLE application APP-2024-0273 are already staged; read them for turbine data and capacity. Case U-22168 says Unit 1 converted to gas in 2025, the whole plant becomes a gas peaker by the end of 2026 at 1,270 MW summer net, owned 81.39% by DTE Electric and 18.61% by the Michigan Public Power Agency, and retires in 2039. Check the owner shares and the planned retirement.

L100000103983.text: Lansing Board of Water and Light. The validation report says Owner 1 has no Owners Data Source. Find a document naming the owner (the utility's own pages, EIA-860, or the EGLE permit) and stage the source. Check whether this record is the Erickson plant, the Eckert plant or the REO Town cogeneration plant, and whether it duplicates Delta energy park.

L100000402461.text: Delta energy park. The RICE_set unit has no Other IDs and EIA-860M shows a status that differs from GEM's. Check the engine set's status, capacity, engine make and model and start year in the EGLE permit and the Lansing Board of Water and Light releases.

L100001083332.text: Bay County power station, Consumers Energy, 450 MW, pre-construction with an approximate location and unknown technology. The point is on the Karn and Weadock site in Hampton Township. Read the 2026 Consumers Energy plan filing and any EGLE permit application for the turbine type, capacity, site and in-service year, and settle the status from the status ladder. Check the MISO queue for a matching entry. The Consumers Energy plan filed in 2026 (Case U-22127) names a 456 MW simple cycle plant at the Karn site in Essexville; read it for the turbine make, start year and the certificate of necessity status.

L100001083333.text: Genesee County power station, Consumers Energy, 900 MW, pre-construction with an approximate location and unknown technology. Read the 2026 Consumers Energy plan filing, the MISO queue and any EGLE permit application for the site, technology, capacity and in-service year. Check whether it is tied to a data center customer. Case U-22127 names a 919 MW simple cycle plant at the Thetford site in Genesee County; use it for the site, capacity and technology.

L100001082478.text: Handy Township power station, near Fowlerville in Livingston County, 1400 MW, owner listed as DTE Energy Co. A 2018 article says a firm proposed a 1 billion dollar gas plant there. Find out who the developer is now and whether it is DTE Electric Co or another company, using entity_lookup.py before any owner change. Check the start year: the Environmental Integrity Project says 2032, GEM says 2031. Check whether the project is still alive or should be shelved or cancelled under the manual's rules, and whether it appears in a DTE plan, given that its IRP box is ticked. The DTE Electric plan filed in 2026 (Case U-22168) calls it the Livingston County Project: about 1,400 MW combined cycle in Handy Township, two single shaft trains, in service by the end of 2031, built ready for carbon capture. Use it for the technology, owner and date.

L100001088928.text: Milan Township power station, DTE Electric, 700 MW, pre-construction with an approximate location. Find the site, technology, MISO queue entry and in-service year. Check whether it is the combined cycle DTE plans to replace the Monroe coal plant, or a plant tied to a data center contract, and whether any EGLE permit application exists. Case U-22168 calls it the Monroe County Project: about 700 MW combined cycle in Milan Township, in service by the end of 2032, with MISO queue entries J4024 and J4025.

L100000407415.text: MEC North power station, Development Partners Group, near Marshall in Calhoun County. The Environmental Integrity Project says start 2028, GEM says 2034. Find the newest dated source for the in-service year, the EGLE permit status, the MISO queue entry and whether the Marshall data center and gas plant proposal on the possible-updates sheet is the same project or a separate one.

L100000407414.text: MEC South power station, the sister of MEC North near Marshall. The Environmental Integrity Project says start 2028, GEM says 2034. Research with MEC North and settle the start year and status from dated sources.

L100000402123.text: New Covert generating facility. Check the owner: GEM says New Covert Generating Co LLC with ArcLight parents. Consumers Energy has been buying merchant plants; check EIA-860 ownership, MPSC dockets and company releases for a sale since 2023. Run entity_lookup.py before staging any owner change. Case U-21090 approved the purchase by Consumers Energy on or about May 31, 2023 for 815 million dollars. Confirm the closing and stage the owner change.

L100000402454.text: Dearborn Industrial Generation. Check the owner against EIA-860 and the MPSC record, since Consumers Energy or CMS has been buying merchant plants. The Sierra Club list shows a 271 MW gas turbine cogeneration row as terminated: find out whether a unit here was retired or cancelled, with a primary source. Case U-21090 and later filings say Consumers Energy bought Dearborn Industrial Generation in 2025. Confirm the closing and stage the owner change.

L100000401831.text: Zeeland generating station. EIA-860M gives 188.7 MW for unit 1A, GEM says 239 MW. A closed database comment from Jenny Martos in May 2025 says Consumers expected a 50 MW upgrade in June 2025. Find a source for the upgrade and the current nameplate generating MW of each unit.

L100000401674.text: Michigan power station (Michigan Power Cogeneration, Ludington, 138 MW, listed under Osaka Gas). Case U-22168 says DTE Electric will buy it from its affiliate DTE Sustainable Generation in 2030 for 130 million dollars. Check who owns it now, since the filing implies DTE Sustainable Generation and not Osaka Gas, and run entity_lookup.py before any owner change.

L100000409204.text: Case U-21081 says A.J. Mihm is three Wartsila 18V50SG engines, 54.9 MW net. Check unit split, engine model and capacity.

L100000409210.text: Case U-21081 and U-21542 give F.D. Kuester as 125.6 MW, running 2019 to 2049. Check capacity and engine model.
